summary:
1)WHAT WE DEVELOPED: "I Am Astronut", an interactive web-based aerospace simulation and planetary exploration game. Powered by an HTML5 Canvas physics engine, React 18 HUD, and Three.js 3D WebGL, it simulates real-time orbital mechanics, celestial gravity, and verified NASA telemetry across six destinations, spotlighting the historic Lunar South Pole (80∘S Malapert A).

2)HOW IT ADDRESS THE CHALLENGE: Traditional space education often suffers from high mathematical entry barriers or passive textbook memorization. Our game gamifies complex aerospace concepts—such as rocket staging, delta-v (Δ𝑣), and planetary atmospheres—into intuitive gameplay. Players begin on Earth as space cadets searching for hidden rocket hardware while dodging dynamic meteor hazards, earning promotion to astronaut for deep-space missions upon assembly.




3)WHY IS IT IMPORTANT: It democratizes STEM education by running dependency-free in any browser with offline Progressive Web App (PWA) support, making high-fidelity space science accessible on low-spec classroom devices. By protecting student privacy through offline teacher keys and celebrating global milestones—including planting the Indian Flag (Tiranga 🇮🇳) alongside NASA achievements—it inspires the next generation of space scientists and engineers.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

  • Terrestrial Staging & Scavenger Mechanics: The game starts on Earth at Kennedy Space Center LC-39A, where players on foot explore the launch complex, dodge kinetic meteor showers, and locate three hidden rocket modules (Fuselage, Engine Bell, and Guidance Avionics) guided by holographic light pillars and distance radar.
  • Deep-Space Orbital Exploration: Once the rocket is assembled, the cadet is promoted to flight astronaut, unlocking vertical ascent to verified NASA destinations (such as the Lunar South Pole, Apollo 11, and Mars), where players conduct surface EVAs, plant the Indian Flag (Tiranga 🇮🇳), and inspect 3D terrain with a laser spectrometer.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Intuitive STEM Pedagogy: Replaces passive textbook memorization by turning complex aerospace principles—such as gravitational acceleration , escape velocity, delta-v (Δv\Delta vΔv), and atmospheric drag—into hands-on, gamified mechanics.
  • Universal Zero-Barrier Access: Operates instantly inside any modern web browser across low-spec classroom Chromebooks, laptops, tablets, and smartphones without software installations, subscription fees, or dedicated graphics hardware.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Democratization of Aerospace Education: Empowers resource-constrained schools and educators to provide high-fidelity space science simulations to students at zero software cost.
  • Inspiring Future Space Scientists: Fosters deep scientific curiosity and national pride by showcasing real-world milestones (NASA Artemis, Apollo, and India's space achievements) to inspire the next generation of engineers.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Frontend Stack & Libraries: Built using standard HTML5 Canvas (60 FPS custom physics), JavaScript (ES6+), React 18 (declarative micro-HUD), Three.js (WebGL 3D surface inspector), and Tailwind CSS (responsive sci-fi glassmorphism).
  • Web APIs & Development Environment: Leveraged the Web Audio API for procedural sound synthesis, Service Worker API (PWA offline caching v15), LocalStorage for secure client-side state saves, and developed on standard consumer PCs.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Emotional Cadet-to-Astronaut Narrative: Rather than spawning immediately as a rocket in space, players begin grounded as an aspiring boy or girl cadet who must prove their resilience under falling asteroid hazards to earn their flight suit and the title "I Am Astronaut".
  • Hybrid 2D/3D Dual-Engine Architecture: Seamlessly merges high-velocity 2D platforming action (evading meteors and managing jetpack fuel) with an on-demand, interactive 3D WebGL geological scanner that models realistic planetary lighting and mineral composition.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Astrophysical Fidelity & NASA Standards: Calibrated all planetary gravity (1.00g1.00g1.00g on Earth, 0.165g0.165g0.165g on the Moon, 0.38g0.38g0.38g on Mars), atmospheric densities, and coordinates directly against verified NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) archives, spotlighting the historic 80.13∘S80.13^\circ\text{S}80.13∘S Lunar South Pole landing.
  • User Inclusivity & Student Privacy: Implemented three difficulty modes (Easy, Moderate, Difficult) with non-destructive resets, customizable boy/girl personas, and offline "Teacher/Student Keys" that eliminate the need to collect student email addresses or private personal data.
